critical_code_review_comments: articles.get_article: ObjectId(article_id) raises inside try, returns None -> 404 (good). But list_articles projection includes body_md but truncates only after fetch — for 300 docs with 60KB body this is O(n) memory. Consider $substrCP projection to trim server-side.

articles._out.can_edit: admin can edit ANY public article (including notes turned public by other admins) and can delete same. Consistent with spec ('admin curates public'). Confirm this is intended when multiple admins exist.

articles.update_article: does not enforce that a private->public transition preserves original author_id (admin can silently publish any user's private note by editing? No — the doc.author_id != user.id check blocks admins from touching private user notes, and the admin bypass only applies when doc.visibility=='public'. Correct.)
articles.ai_draft: uses datetime.now().timestamp() (naive/local time) for session_id — fine for uniqueness, but consider datetime.now(timezone.utc) for consistency.

articles.py line 220: md.lstrip('markdown') is a character-set strip (removes any of m,a,r,k,d,o,w,n from the start), not a prefix strip. If the model returns e.g. '```markdown\n# x' it will strip the trailing '\n#'. Rare because system prompt says no code fences, but consider md.removeprefix('markdown').
articles.list_articles: no pagination (hard limit 300). At scale this needs a cursor/skip+limit. Non-blocking for MVP.
articles.py imports emergentintegrations INSIDE ai_draft handler — good for cold-start speed, keeps route usable if lib missing.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (anon list+detail+back, admin CRUD, non-admin private note CRUD, regression on /, /watchlist, /movers, /brokers)
